item.title: Windows Grab-Bag: SIGTERM That Doesn't Exist and Sparse Files That Break Docker
item.description:
Two short ones from the Windows node of ephemerd from the last few weeks. Neither is complicated once you know what’s going on. Both took longer than they should have to find, because the failure showed up a long way from the cause.

Part 1: there is no SIGTERM on Windows

ephemerd can run a Cloudflare tunnel so GitHub webhooks reach a node behind NAT. It does that by running cloudflared as a managed subprocess. On Linux the child is tied to ephemerd’s lifetime by the kernel with Pdeathsig:

item.title: shipmates Short Ones: 8 Minutes Extracting Go, and Three Voice-Loop Bugs
item.description:
A few shipmates bugs don’t need a whole post each. They were too good to leave in commit messages, though.

setup-go spends 8 minutes extracting Go on Windows CI

shipmates CI runs on my own ephemerd runners. On Windows those jobs run inside a Hyper-V utility VM. The windows-x64 leg kept timing out in actions/setup-go. Here’s the log from PR #48:

20:58:46  Setup go version spec 1.26.6
20:58:46  Attempting to download 1.26.6...     <- tool-cache MISS
20:58:48  Acquiring 1.26.6 from ...zip
20:58:53  Extracting Go...
21:06:46  ERROR: The action 'Run actions/setup-go@v5' has timed out after 8 minutes

Seven seconds from the start of the step to Extracting Go.... Then almost eight minutes extracting until the step timeout killed it.

item.title: Free Blog Hosting Using Hugo + Github Pages
item.description:
Since I just rode this merry-go-round here is a quick overview of how you can get a professional looking personal blog with custom DNS. It takes minimal effort, costs nothing and runs completely out of a single Github Repository.

Prerequisites

You’ll need to do your own homework on how to use Hugo. You should have a Github account and a decent understanding of using git and getting changes committed and pushed to a repo. You should also have a domain and know how to do some basic DNS changes. The only thing you likely can’t get for free is a domain name, since registrars charge registration costs. But you can get introductory $0.99USD domains for the first year if you shop around and don’t care what TLD you end up with. For reference, luth.io cost me $30/year to register with CloudFlare.
